messages:
anna: Heads-up — intermittent tracebacks popping up in apps that use uvloop + our AsyncClient as a module-global. Happens during shutdown under load.

devon: Can you paste the traceback + a tiny repro?

anna: minimal repro below. app installs uvloop then creates AsyncClient at import time, uses asyncio.run to drive main. sometimes aclose fails: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed.
```python
import uvloop
from redwood import AsyncClient
uvloop.install()
client = AsyncClient()  # module-scope

async def main():
    async with client:
        await client.generate("ping")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(main())
```

lee: That looks like the client (or httpx transport) was created bound to the loop at import time and then aclose is invoked after asyncio.run tears down the loop. We hit this pattern in a different repo too.

maya (devex): Confirmed. httpx backend/transport objects capture the running loop when they are eagerly created. If the SDK instantiates transport in AsyncClient.__init__, closing it from a later/different loop triggers RuntimeError.

anna: Weirdness: older SDK release didn't show this for our codebase. Not sure if a recent change started creating transport eagerly.

devon: Quick fixes: 1) doc warning "don't create AsyncClient at import time with asyncio.run/uvloop" 2) lazy-init transport on first await or in __aenter__ 3) make aclose robust to EventLoopClosed during interpreter shutdown (log at debug, swallow).

lee: We should avoid swallowing errors silently though. Suggest: if EventLoopClosed during process shutdown, log at debug and suppress; otherwise re-raise. Detect interpreter shutdown via sys.is_finalizing() maybe.

maya (devex): Action plan: I will open an internal issue: "sdk: defer httpx transport creation for AsyncClient" with proposed fixes: - create transport in __aenter__ or on first I/O - add helper get_global_async_client() that lazily constructs the client safely - add unit test that runs uvloop + asyncio.run + module-scope client to assert no noisy traceback on exit.

anna: Also hit a flaky test locally: "ValueError: There is no current event loop" when pytest-asyncio + uvloop plugin used. Might be related to get_event_loop/get_running_loop differences in py3.10+.

devon: Good note. Use asyncio.get_running_loop() inside coroutines; avoid get_event_loop() in library init. For detection heuristics at init: if not asyncio.get_event_loop().is_running() is fragile across versions. Better pattern: don't touch any loop at import time.

lee: Another possible ergonomics addition: expose an async context manager factory e.g. AsyncClient.for_app() or a sync factory that returns a lazy proxy. That gives obvious pattern for reuse without surprising loop binding.

maya (devex): Agreed. I'll include API suggestions in the issue: - AsyncClient(lazy_transport=True) opt-in for backwards compatibility - redwood.get_global_async_client() which creates client on first async use - docs quickstart note about module-scope clients and asyncio.run/uvloop.

anna: I'll draft a tiny dockerized repro for the issue and attach CI logs. Happy to help with a unit test.

ci-bot: CI: devex/async-client-lazy-init branch build passed : white_check_mark:

devon: One more edge-case: interpreter-level cleanup can call __del__ of global objects when loop already closed. Maybe implement __del__ to call aclose() only if loop is running or if not sys.is_finalizing(); otherwise skip. Document behavior.

maya (devex): Good catch. We'll be careful to avoid noisy traceback during import/exit. I'll coordinate with runtime team for the fix and schedule a small SDK patch release.

anna: thanks all, appreciate the quick triage. I'll post the repro and link the issue once created. :smile:
